user.title: Loki — terms of use
user.description:
**Read this before setting up.**

**1. You need a separate phone number.** The service allows only one active session per number. Entering a number that is already in use by the operator's mobile app **will sign that app out**. Get a separate number for Home Assistant and add it to the allowed-numbers list through the official app.

**2. Independent project.** Loki is free, open-source software under the MIT licence. It is not an official product of any intercom operator, is not affiliated with or supported by one. All trademarks belong to their respective owners.

**3. No warranty.** The software is provided "AS IS", without warranty of any kind. **It is not a security device** and is not a replacement for the standard means of access. The author is not liable for any damages arising from use of, or inability to use, the software.

**4. Your responsibility.** You must have lawful access to the intercom system and to the account used. You are responsible for assessing whether your use complies with your agreement with the operator, and for complying with data-protection law when using video and face recognition.

**5. Data.** Loki runs locally. The author receives and stores nothing: not your number, confirmation codes, tokens, or video.

phone.title: Phone number
phone.description:
Enter the phone number registered to the flat.

⚠️ Reminder: if this number is in use by the operator's mobile app, that app will be signed out.

sms.title: Confirmation
sms.description:
Enter the code sent by SMS to {phone}.

The code is valid for about 20 minutes. If no SMS arrived, tick "Resend the code" and submit.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description:
The session for {phone} has ended.

There are two possible reasons: the token expired (this happens routinely and is expected), or **someone signed in elsewhere with this same number** — the service allows only one active session per number.

⚠️ If another device took the session, signing in here will **sign that device out**. If this keeps happening, get a separate number for Home Assistant and add it through the official app.

Submit to receive a new code by SMS.

panel.title: Ready-made page
panel.description:
Add a **Домофоны** page to the sidebar — every door as a tile with an open button under it?

It is a sidebar entry of its own and does not touch your dashboards. You can turn it off later in the integration options.

The cards appear in the card picker either way.

reconfigure.title: Sign in by SMS again
reconfigure.description:
Currently using **{phone}**.

Enter a phone number — an SMS code will be sent to it.

- **The same number** is a fresh sign-in: it renews the session and the SIP credentials. This is what clears the “the registrar refused” card.
- **A different number** moves this entry to another account. Doors and cameras are kept: their device cards are keyed on the intercom system's own ids, not on the phone number. A number another Loki entry already uses cannot be taken — the service allows one session per number.

⚠️ SIP credentials are issued per number. If the service returns the same SIP identity, the SIP state is kept and registration comes back at once; if it returns a different one, Loki starts afresh and spends about ten minutes watching the account again before it registers.

data_description.phone: Any format: +7 999 123-45-67, 8 999 1234567, 9991234567. The same number just means a fresh sign-in.

data_description.scan_interval: Doors and cameras change rarely, so polling often gains nothing.
data_description.sip_strict_guard: Do not register while somebody else holds a binding on the SIP account. Turning this off removes the only check that prevents rather than detects: the intercom may stop ringing the resident's phone.
data_description.sidebar_panel: A sidebar entry showing every intercom. Your dashboards are left alone.

open_door.name: Open door
open_door.description: Opens a door by its device id. Needed for automations where the id arrives in a call event.

simulate_ring.name: Simulate a ring
simulate_ring.description: Fires an incoming-call event for a door, to test notifications and automations without a real intercom call.

hangup.name: End call
hangup.description: Ends the active call for a door.

capture_frame.name: Capture current frame
capture_frame.description: Takes one frame from the intercom's video stream and makes it the current picture. Needed because the server's own snapshot is static and does not show what is happening now. Requires access to the video stream.

device_id.name: Device id
device_id.description: Numeric id of the door or camera.

confirm.title: Set the account up again
confirm.description:
The stored data for account "{title}" holds no phone number, so signing in again is impossible — there is nothing to sign in with.

Submit to remove the entry, then add the integration again via "Add integration → Loki". Your devices and their identifiers are preserved.

sip_terminal_blocked.title: Loki: SIP not started — account “{title}” is in use
sip_terminal_blocked.description:
Another device is already registered on the SIP account. Loki did not register, because doing so could displace that binding and the intercom would stop ringing the phone with nothing to show for it.

Details: {detail}

**There is probably nothing to do.** Most often this is Loki's own binding from before a restart: it lives a few minutes and lapses by itself. Loki checks the account again and registers as soon as it is free — see `sensor.*_sip_status`, which also shows how long there is left to wait.

**If this lasts more than ten minutes**, another device really is on the account, almost certainly a phone running the operator's app. Get a separate phone number for Home Assistant and add it to the allowed numbers in the official app.

If you understand the risk and want to register anyway, turn off the strict check in the integration options.

sip_terminal_evicted.title: Loki: SIP stopped — registering displaced another device
sip_terminal_evicted.description:
A binding that was not ours disappeared after we registered. Loki withdrew its own registration and stopped.

Details: {detail}

**Check that the intercom still rings the phone.** If it does not, restart the operator's app on the phone and it will register again.

Do not turn SIP back on until Home Assistant has a phone number of its own, or the same thing will happen.

sip_terminal_rejected.title: Loki: SIP is not working — the registrar refused account “{title}”

sip_terminal_failed.title: Loki: SIP stopped for account “{title}”
